summary: Ji-yong Kim works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 1976, Kim held professorships at both Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at Nankai University and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello. He was attested as Professor at the University of Arizona from 2011 to 2018.
Jianming Hu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University, attested in 2015. In that same year, Hu held a post as a researcher at Komazawa University.

Jien Abe (1937–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). Until 2001, Abe served as a professor at Meiji University.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi. Junu also studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi (1915–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a member at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and held a professorship at Rissho University.

Jikido Takasaki (1926–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned PhDs from Savitribai Phule Pune University and the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1977–1987) and president of Tsurumi University (1992–2004).
Jim G. Shaffer is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Arizona State University (~1962–1968) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1972).

Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hamburg and a PhD from the University of the West of England (by 2008) and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

Jim Taylor specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from Macquarie University by 1989, he served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.

Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Park was an assistant professor of philosophy and religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and served as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jinah Kim specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams. Kim held posts at Vanderbilt University, the Institute for Advanced Study (2009–2010), and Harvard University.

Jinbo Shi is a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology who studied at Minzu University of China (~1958–1962). He held posts at CASS's Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology (~1966–2005) and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–2010).
Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2010, Wan was attested as a professor at both National Central University and Fo Guang University.
Jing Yin specializes in Buddhist studies and studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). Between 2006 and 2010, Yin was attested as Director at the University of Hong Kong.

Jing-shen Tao is a sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University. He was a fellow at Academia Sinica (attested 1995) and Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).
Jingkong (1927–2022) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Thomé H. Fang from ~1953 to 1954 and under Bingnan Li from ~1958 to 1968.

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. After graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research under Noritoshi Aramaki at Kyoto University, Chen held positions at the University of Virginia (attested 2001) and the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia works in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Jia earned a PhD from the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll, and has held posts at City University of Hong Kong and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
Jinling He specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Koki Okumura.
